title: Don Wakamatsu praises Ulsan Fall League for boosting Korean player development
text:
Don Wakamatsu praises Ulsan Fall League for boosting Korean player development - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 29일(목) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Don Wakamatsu praises Ulsan Fall League for boosting Korean player development 
 입력 2026.10.28. 13:30 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 "It's moving in the right direction."
 The Ulsan-KBO Fall League (hereinafter Fall League), hosted by the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) and sponsored by Ulsan Metropolitan City and the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, marks its third year. It was launched inspired by development leagues that attract prospects, such as Japan's Miyazaki Phoenix League and the U.S. Arizona Fall League. The Fall League was created thanks to Ulsan city's full support and the active will of KBO president Heo Gu-yeon, and it is running smoothly.
 As it reaches its third year, the scale of the tournament has steadily grown. The inaugural 2024 tournament featured eight teams: KBO League futures teams, a Korean independent league all-star team, a Mexican league all-star team, SoftBank's third squad from Japan, and the Cuba national team, which at the time was preparing for the Premier12 tournament. Teams from the Chinese professional league were also invited. In the second edition in 2025, 11 teams participated. In addition to domestic teams, Australia Professional Baseball, a Japanese independent league, and a university all-star team took part.
 Efforts continued to develop the Fall League into a more international competition. This year, six domestic KBO League teams and the Ulsan Whales participated, along with a Korean independent league all-star team. Overseas participants included a Japanese independent league team, the Melbourne Aces from Australian professional baseball, the Jiangsu team from China Professional Baseball, and the Long Beach Breakers from the Pioneer League, an independent league partnered with Major League Baseball. A record 12 teams competed for supremacy.
 The Pioneer League, based in the U.S. West and the Rocky Mountain region, was once run as a minor league affiliated with major league clubs. The 2020 season was canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and the minor league system underwent a major reorganization. However, in 2021 it converted to an independent league and has continued as an MLB partner league.
 The Long Beach Breakers participating in the Ulsan Fall League are managed by Don Wakamatsu, who has major league managerial experience. He managed the Seattle Mariners in 2009–2010. A fourth-generation Japanese American, he was the first Asian manager in major league history.
 Even after stepping down from a managerial position, he continued his coaching career as a bench coach for Toronto, Kansas City, Texas and others. Since 2023, he has served as vice president of Innovation Baseball Partners, one of the operating entities of teams participating in the Pioneer League, while also serving as manager of the Long Beach Breakers.
 A coach seasoned in the major leagues is participating in a nascent development league across the Pacific. Wakamatsu said he "likes to travel and it's my first visit to Korea, but I was happy when I learned I had the opportunity to participate in the Ulsan Fall League," adding, "I did not expect it to be as grand as major league standards, but I was very pleased with the opportunities and facilities for our players to showcase their talents and with the hospitality of the KBO. KBO's support was first-rate."
 The Pioneer League season had already ended, so deciding to join another league in an unfamiliar place was probably not easy. Wakamatsu said, "We have a philosophy of recruiting players so our players can have opportunities to play at a higher level while still being able to win," and added, "Playing here against KBO, Australian and Japanese teams will be an excellent experience for our young players to grow both on and off the field."
 What kind of league is the Pioneer League? We asked Wakamatsu to explain. He said, "The U.S. independent leagues have a very long history. In the past they were close to amateur, but that is no longer the case," and began, "After Major League Baseball started reducing minor league teams, competitiveness has increased significantly."
 He continued, "With the draft shrinking to nearly 20 rounds, there are about 600 undrafted players. Many players who under normal circumstances would have been drafted have flowed into independent leagues, raising the overall level."
 In fact, Long Beach is recording the best results in the Fall League. As of the 27th, they are undefeated with a 9-game record of 7 wins and 2 ties. An official who watched Long Beach's games said, "There are many full-time players and the level is higher than expected. The pitchers' velocity and movement are both solid. There seem to be pitchers who could potentially play in the KBO League."
 Catcher Thomas McCaffrey, who has played two years with Long Beach, explained, "Pitchers often want to throw hard to earn contracts with major league clubs and gain recognition. As for hitters, many focus more on power hitting."
 He also found the Fall League's level to reflect its role as a development league. Wakamatsu said, "The level here is really good. We're experiencing a slightly different baseball style. We're seeing Asian-style baseball, such as and-run, bunt strategies and slide steps," and added, "Another surprising point is that Asian players' physiques are becoming much stronger and bigger." McCaffrey also said, "I think it's competitive. I've been telling players the league level is quite high," describing his impressions of the Fall League as a player.
 "The KBO is a healthy league, and the fan base in Korea is young, mainly in their 20s and 30s. Both the U.S. and Japan are struggling to secure young fans, but Korea is different," Wakamatsu said, adding, "Moreover, having young players on the field is important, and Korea could have tremendous power over the next 10 years."
 He also made recommendations for the development of the Ulsan Fall League. He said, "I've heard talks about Taiwanese teams participating in the future, and I've heard that more U.S. teams want to join. I think the Ulsan Fall League is moving in the right direction," stressing, "It will help KBO players' growth to meet internationally talented players. Seeing diverse playing styles can also contribute to a player's development." [OSEN]
